channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Kazakhstan President Dismisses Three Senior Defense Ministry Officials
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has dismissed three high-ranking officials from the Ministry of Defense. The dismissals follow the tragic incident during military exercises in the Caspian Sea where 14 servicemen died.

item.title: Kazakh President Dismisses Several High-Ranking Defense Officials
item.description: By order of the Head of State, several officials from the Ministry of Defense have been dismissed. This includes the First Deputy Minister of Defense - Chief of the General Staff, a Deputy Minister of Defense, and the Commander-in-Chief of the Naval Forces.

item.title: Kazakh President Tokayev Dismisses Three Senior Military Officials
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has dismissed three high-ranking military officials. The exact reasons for the dismissals were not immediately specified, but they follow recent events within the armed forces.

item.title: Kazakh President Dismisses Three Senior Defense Ministry Officials
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has dismissed three high-ranking officials from the Ministry of Defense. The specific reasons for the dismissals were not immediately disclosed by the presidential administration.

item.title: Cost of Paid Military Service This Year Stands at 58,500 Somoni
item.description: The cost of paid or alternative military service this year is 58,500 somoni, equivalent to 750 indexation units. To be included in the list of individuals eligible for paid service, applicants must contact military commissariats.

item.title: Further Dismissals Occur Within the Ministry of Defense
item.description: The wave of dismissals within the Ministry of Defense continues. President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev removed Kanysh Abdukirov, First Deputy Minister of Defense and Chief of the General Staff, Almaz Jumakeyev, Deputy Minister of Defense, and Kanat Niyazbekov, Commander-in-Chief of the Naval Forces.

item.title: Kazakhstan President Replaces Top Military Officials Amidst Investigation
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has dismissed the Chief of the General Staff, a Deputy Defense Minister, and the Commander of the Naval Forces. These changes follow the death of 14 servicemen during Caspian Sea exercises. A criminal investigation into negligence is underway, and a commission is reviewing the Ministry of Defense's operations.

item.title: Kazakhstan MFA Addresses Citizens Recruited for Ukraine Conflict
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Foreign Affairs has issued a statement regarding citizens allegedly recruited under false pretenses to fight in Ukraine. The ministry is taking the situation seriously and has established a hotline for relatives seeking assistance. Protecting citizens abroad is a top priority.

item.title: Kazakhstan President Dismisses Three Senior Defense Ministry Officials
item.description: Kazakhstan's President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has dismissed three high-ranking officials from the Ministry of Defense. This follows a recent tragedy on the Caspian Sea where 14 servicemen died. The president has ordered a comprehensive military reform to enhance security and readiness.

item.title: Iran's IRGC Quds Force Commander Calls for Strengthening Regional Defense Belt
item.description: Esmail Qaani, commander of Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps Quds Force, urged strengthening a "belt of defense, independence and dignity" stretching from Afghanistan to Yemen. He made these remarks at a ceremony in Tehran, emphasizing the need for enhanced regional security cooperation.

item.title: UAE Prosecution Investigates Flydubai Pilot's Attack as Attempted Terrorist Act
item.description: The UAE Public Prosecution is investigating the incident involving a flydubai pilot attacking the captain as an attempted terrorist act. The co-pilot allegedly used an emergency axe to seize control of the aircraft during a flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv. Investigations into motives and connections are ongoing.

item.title: Kazakh President Proposes Global Adoption of AI Accord Based on 'Washington Model'
item.description: Kazakhstan's President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev advocates for the global adoption of an AI accord, inspired by the 'Washington Model' signed by U.S. tech leaders. He proposed this at the AI Development Council, suggesting it could form the basis of a UN treaty and announced Kazakhstan's intention to present its vision at the G20 Summit.

item.title: Doctor Arrested in Connection with Death of 13-Year-Old Boy in Mangystau
item.description: A surgeon from the regional children's hospital has been arrested six months after the death of 13-year-old Ismail Azanov in Aktau. An investigation by the Ministry of Health found the boy was refused admission four times and received inadequate care. He later died after complications from surgery.

item.title: Saida Mirziyoyeva Reports Meeting with Donald Trump, Provides No Details
item.description: Saida Mirziyoyeva, daughter of Uzbekistan's president, announced a meeting with Donald Trump on social media, accompanied by a photo. She expressed pride in the conversation. Details regarding the date and location were not disclosed, and the White House has not commented.

item.title: Iran Executes Five Afghan Citizens in September, Human Rights Group Reports
item.description: The Hengaw Human Rights Organization reported that Iran executed five Afghan citizens in September. A total of 68 prisoners were executed across Iran last month, a decrease of 23.5% from August. The primary charges for the executed Afghan nationals were drug trafficking and murder. Afghan citizens constitute the largest group of foreign prisoners in Iran.

item.title: Kazakhstan to integrate artificial intelligence into secondary education system
item.description: Kazakhstan has unveiled a project to implement artificial intelligence in its secondary education system. The initiative, presented to President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev, aims to assist teachers and personalize learning. The Ministry of Education emphasizes that AI will supplement, not replace, educators, enhancing educational quality, especially in rural schools.

item.title: Kazakhstan Restores Hearing for 169 Children with Implants in First Half of Year
item.description: In the first half of 2026, Kazakh doctors restored hearing for 169 children using high-tech cochlear implants, with most surgeries performed on children under five. The state allocated 1.8 billion tenge for these procedures. Early detection and treatment are crucial for speech and auditory development.

item.title: Kazakhstan Developing Digital Infrastructure at Advanced Pace, Says Prime Minister Olzhas Bektenov
item.description: Prime Minister Olzhas Bektenov reviewed digital solutions presented at the AI & Digital Bridge 2026 forum and presented awards to winners. Domestic companies showcased AI-based developments in education, finance, and industry, including AI tutors, intelligent assistants, and digital twins for industrial applications.

item.title: Flydubai Co-pilot Removed from Duty Over Extremist Views, CNN Reports
item.description: A Flydubai co-pilot, suspected of attacking another pilot on a flight to Tel Aviv, was found with images of Al-Qaeda leaders and radical content online. The Omani national had previously been removed from flight training at Oman Air due to extremist views, according to CNN.

item.title: Afghanistan Faces High Casualties from Unexploded Ordnance, UN Reports
item.description: Afghanistan remains among countries with the highest casualties from unexploded ordnance (UXO), with 64 incidents and civilian casualties recorded this year. The UN spokesperson stated that UXO poses a serious threat, especially to children. Efforts to clear contaminated areas are hampered by funding shortages.

item.title: Over 60 New Agreements Reached Following AI & Digital Bridge Forum in Astana
item.description: The AI & Digital Bridge 2026 forum in Astana resulted in over 60 new partnership agreements. Kazakhstan's Prime Minister Oljas Bektenov stated the country aims to integrate new technological and digital standards into its economy, emphasizing the need for collaboration between government, science, and international tech companies. The forum also highlighted the Data Center Valley project.

item.title: Personal Data of Over 500 Teachers Leaked Online in Kyzylorda Region
item.description: Personal data of over 500 teachers was found in open access in the Kyzylorda region, according to the regional prosecutor's office. The data was posted on the state procurement portal as part of documents for medical examination services. Disciplinary action was taken against education officials responsible for the leak.

item.title: Kazakh Citizen Wanted for Five Years Extradited from Abroad
item.description: A citizen of Kazakhstan, who had been on an international wanted list since 2021, has been brought to Astana. The National Security Committee reported that the individual is suspected of large-scale fraud and had been evading law enforcement since 2021. The suspect has been detained.

item.title: Over 900 Afghan Migrants Return to the Country Through Border Crossings
item.description: The Taliban announced that 971 Afghan migrants, including 219 families, returned to Afghanistan through various border crossings on Friday. Hamdullah Fitrat, a Taliban spokesperson, provided figures for returns via Torkham, Pul-e Abrishum, Spin Boldak, and Islam Qala. UN and aid groups expressed concern about the impact on Afghanistan's capacity.

item.title: UAE Prosecutor General: Flydubai Co-pilot Intended Terrorist Act
item.description: The UAE's Prosecutor General stated that investigations into a Flydubai incident revealed the co-pilot attempted a terrorist act. During the flight, the co-pilot attacked the captain with an emergency axe in the cockpit, attempting to seize control of the aircraft. The plane, with 182 passengers, was reportedly brought to the brink of crashing due to the co-pilot's actions.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Foreign Ministry Responds to Citizens' Requests for Repatriation
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Foreign Affairs has responded to requests from citizens seeking assistance to return to their homeland. The ministry's reaction indicates a process is underway to address the repatriation needs of Kazakh citizens abroad. Further details on the nature of the response or specific actions taken were not immediately available.

item.title: Tajikistan Discusses Implementation of Four Strategic Development Programs
item.description: Tajikistan's Ministry of Economic Development and Trade reviewed the progress of four strategic planning documents focusing on green economy, education, кадровая политика, and tourism. The meeting, held on October 1, 2026, involved representatives from relevant ministries and departments. Decisions were made to ensure timely implementation of planned activities.

item.title: Child surgeon arrested in Aktau following patient's death, police explain
item.description: A pediatric surgeon has been arrested in Aktau after a child patient died. Police in the Mangystau region stated the doctor is suspected of professional negligence. According to investigators, errors in diagnosis and treatment at the regional hospital may have contributed to complications. The child was airlifted to Almaty but could not be saved.

item.title: Iran Urges Iraq to Lift Restrictions on its Airlines Amid US Sanctions
item.description: Iran's Foreign Ministry has called on Iraq to act independently of US sanctions and lift restrictions on air travel between the two countries. Iran stated that these restrictions harm passengers and contradict the strategic relationship based on good neighborliness. Iran considers US sanctions illegal and a violation of national sovereignty.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Lower Age of Criminal Responsibility for Group Hooliganism to 14
item.description: Uzbekistan will lower the age of criminal responsibility for hooliganism committed in an organized group from 16 to 14 years. The law also introduces responsibility for creating and financing criminal organizations, and toughens penalties for hooliganism and intentional infliction of grievous bodily harm. Criminal liability for illegal martial arts competitions is also introduced.

item.title: Aircraft "Voris" reaches Dushanbe on second attempt after Turkmenistan denied airspace
item.description: The aircraft "Voris" has arrived in Dushanbe on its second attempt after Turkmenistan denied it permission to cross its airspace. The flight rerouted and proceeded to its destination, bypassing Turkmen airspace. This marks a deviation from the initial flight plan and airspace clearance.

item.title: UAE prosecutor's office officially labels FlyDubai flight incident an attempted terrorist act
item.description: The UAE Attorney General's office has officially classified the incident on a FlyDubai flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv as an attempted terrorist act. The co-pilot allegedly attacked the captain with an emergency axe and attempted to seize control of the aircraft. Investigations into the attacker's motives and connections are ongoing.

item.title: International Conference on Central Asia in the 1990s Held in Bishkek
item.description: An international conference dedicated to the socio-political and social transformations of the 1980s-1990s in Central Asian countries is taking place in Bishkek from October 2 to 4. Historians, scholars, and culturologists from the region, including former Kyrgyz President Roza Otunbayeva, are participating. The conference examines the 1990s not only as a period of economic crisis but also as a time of active social processes and struggles for rights.

item.title: Kazakhstan to complete new railway to Uzbekistan by year-end
item.description: Kazakhstan is nearing completion of the 127.6 km Darbaza-Maktaaral railway line, with operations planned by the end of 2026. The new route aims to create an additional corridor to Uzbekistan, ease congestion on the Sariagash-Tashkent section, and expand regional transit capabilities. The project, started in November 2023, is valued at $545 million.

item.title: Kazakhstan MFA urges relatives to provide data on citizens in conflict zones
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Foreign Affairs has established a hotline for relatives seeking information about Kazakh citizens in conflict zones. The ministry emphasized its commitment to protecting citizens abroad and stated it has experience in repatriating citizens from various global conflict areas.

item.title: Central Asia Becoming Predictable Region Amid Global Crises, Says Official
item.description: First Deputy Chairman of the Senate of Uzbekistan, Sodiq Safoyev, stated at a regional forum that Central Asia is becoming a more stable and attractive region despite global crises. He emphasized the need for cooperation, regional identity, and mutual trust for future development.

item.title: Oil Tanker Struck by Unidentified Projectile Off Oman Coast, No Injuries Reported
item.description: An oil tanker was hit by an unidentified projectile approximately four nautical miles east of Oman, according to the UK Maritime Trade Operations. The tanker's captain reported the incident, but no crew members were injured and no environmental damage was sustained. The responsible party remains unclear, though tensions between Iran and the US are high.

item.title: Belgian Interior Minister: Criminal Afghan Migrants Should Be Deported
item.description: Belgium's Interior Minister stated that approximately 60 Afghan nationals with illegal residency, including convicted murderers and rapists, should be deported after serving their sentences. She emphasized that allowing them to remain would be inhumane and urged coalition partners to prioritize returns.

item.title: Zarafshan Glacier in Tajikistan Shrank by 11.7% Over 32 Years
item.description: The Zarafshan glacier basin in Tajikistan has lost 17.5 sq km, or 11.7%, of its ice area between 1992 and 2024, while average temperatures rose by 1 degree Celsius. Researchers attribute this degradation to rising temperatures, changing precipitation, and pollution, warning of further 15-20% shrinkage in 30-40 years.

item.title: Western countries plan to move embassies from Kyiv amid emergency concerns
item.description: Western nations are reportedly planning to relocate their embassies from Kyiv. According to The Guardian, contingency plans are being developed to move diplomatic missions to Lviv or eastern Poland in case of an emergency in Kyiv.
